overview.intro: Ubiquity discovers open-source signals, geotags and verifies them, and turns them into live feeds you can monitor, query and route into existing workflows. The API covers the full lifecycle of that platform: discover, stream and understand.

servers.https://auth.filterlabs.ai: Keycloak auth server (realm filter-labs-web, client web-app)
servers.https://agents.ubiquity.filterlabs.ai: Trial / preview signup site ('Ubiquity for Agents'): signup and health check only

overview.authentication: All endpoints except the token call and the two signup-site calls require a JWT, sent as `Authorization: Bearer ***`. Tokens come from the Keycloak token endpoint (realm filter-labs-web, client web-app) using the password grant, and are renewed with the refresh_token grant. Access tokens last about 30 minutes; refresh tokens last about 8 hours and rotate on use.
families: Pipelines, feeds, entities, jobs, saved searches, sharing, media, direct data stream.
Query parsing, discovery job launch, dataset-upload workflow.
Trial account signup and health check (separate base URL, no token).

conventions.text: **Full replacements.** Several update calls are full replacements, not partial patches. Feed `PUT`, metric generator `PUT` and pipeline `PATCH` (whole `metadata` object) all drop fields you omit, so read the resource first and resend unchanged values.

**Identifiers.** `feed_id`, `entity_id` and entity source ids are integers; `pipeline_id`, `saved_search_id`, `job_id` and `session_id` are strings. For the user id, entity votes take the Keycloak UUID (the JWT `sub` claim) while the chat endpoints and the permissions endpoints take the account email.
**Paging.** List endpoints take `limit` and `offset`. The feed stream is different: it pages with an opaque cursor (returned as `next_cursor`) and has no offset.

status_codes: Success; 201 is returned when a resource is created (pipelines, routes, feeds, saved searches).
Success with an empty body (deletes of routes and metric generators).
Rejected request, for example `POST /pipelines` before its feed exists returns `{"error": "Feed not found"}`.
Not found, for example a media asset that is not stored, or an artifact that does not belong to the feed.
`POST /artifacts/preview` before any artifacts have been ingested (expected at that stage).

workflow.title: Core workflow: creating a pipeline
workflow.lead: Pipeline creation is three ordered calls, each returning an id the next one needs. Launching a discovery job is a separate, optional fourth step.
steps: Save the parsed query and filters.
Create the feed that will hold collected content.
Link the saved search and feed into a new pipeline.
Optional. Start discovery; poll with GET /locations/api/v1/jobs/{job_id}.

sections.heading: Where the inputs come from
sections.text: The query is first parsed by `POST /search/unified`. Its `location.id` becomes the saved search's `search_filters.location_uuid`, its parsed locations, topics and entity types are flattened into `search_filters.entities`, and its `session_id` is passed to `POST /pipelines`.

sections.heading: Importing your own sources
sections.text: Add URLs with `POST /feeds/{feed_id}/sources/upload` (returns 202), or upload a behavioral dataset with `POST /orchestrator/workflows/dataset-upload/trigger` and poll its status endpoint until it completes.

Send `{"message": "..."}` to the session messages endpoint. The call is synchronous, so the reply, including any `filter_update`, comes back in the same response and no polling is needed. The session is created implicitly if it does not exist yet.
sections.heading: Ubi chat in one call
Checking ingestion progress
sections.text: Use `GET /understand/artifacts/count/{feed_id}` for a fast, inexpensive count of ingested artifacts. It is cheaper than reading `total_count` from `artifacts/preview`.

sections.heading: Getting a trial account
sections.text: Send an email address (first and last name are optional) to `POST /api/v1/signup` on the signup site; no token is needed. The call is idempotent: re-submitting an existing email returns the same `user_id` with `created=false` and does not send another invite.

sections.heading: Sharing a pipeline
sections.text: A pipeline can only be shared with members of your own organizations; arbitrary email invites are not supported. List your organizations, list the members of one, then grant access with a `PUT` to the pipeline's permissions.

sections.heading: Reading media
sections.text: Stream items from platforms that capture media carry a `media_assets` list. Pass an asset's ids to the media endpoint to get a presigned download URL that expires after about 5 minutes.

reference_note: Example request bodies use placeholder values in angle brackets; response structures show field names with their types, and `...` where the type is not documented yet.

param_notes.offset: Number of results to skip, for pagination.

groups.name: Authentication
groups.blurb: Keycloak-issued JWTs, sent as a Bearer token on every other call.

groups.name: Trial Signup & Health
groups.blurb: Create a trial account and check service health. Both calls are served by the signup site (a separate base URL) and need no token.

groups.name: Search & Locations
groups.blurb: Turn a free-text query into structured entities and look up places.

groups.name: Pipelines & Routing
groups.blurb: Pipelines tie a saved search to a feed; routes pass results between pipelines.

groups.name: Sharing & Permissions
groups.blurb: Find who a pipeline can be shared with, and manage who has access.

groups.name: Saved Searches & Feeds
groups.blurb: Feeds hold the stream of collected content and its media; metric generators score it.

groups.name: Entities & Review
groups.blurb: Review, vote on, split and remove the sources and datasets Ubiquity discovers.

groups.name: Import Sources
groups.blurb: Bring your own URLs or behavioral datasets into a feed.

groups.name: Discovery Jobs
groups.blurb: Launch, monitor and cancel agentic discovery work.

groups.name: Understand
groups.blurb: Per-feed chat with Ubi, plus artifact and metric data for the Data Browser.

POST /realms/filter-labs-web/protocol/op.desc: Log in or refresh a token (Keycloak password and refresh_token grants).
notes: Send the body form-encoded. Use `grant_type=password` with `username` and `password` to log in, or `grant_type=refresh_token` with `refresh_token` to renew.

200.text: Tokens issued. The access token lasts about 30 minutes; the refresh token about 8 hours and rotates, so always store the newest one.

POST /api/v1/signup.desc: Create a trial / preview account. No token needed; served by the signup site.
notes: Served by the signup site (`https://agents.ubiquity.filterlabs.ai`), not the main backend. No Bearer token is needed.
Idempotent: submitting an email that already has an account returns the same `user_id` with `created` and `invited` false. No second invite is sent and no duplicate is created.
No deliverability or domain check is performed, so a syntactically valid but undeliverable address is created the same as a real one.

fields.first_name: Optional. Omit the field entirely when blank; do not send an empty string.

200.text: Account created, or already existing. `created` and `invited` are both true only for a genuinely new signup.

GET /health.desc: Health check for the signup site's backend. No token needed.
notes: Served by the signup site (`https://agents.ubiquity.filterlabs.ai`), not the main backend. No Bearer token is needed.
The signup API is hosted as part of the Scout search service, which is the service name reported here.

200.text: Service status.

POST /orchestrator/search/unified.desc: Parse a free-text query into location, topic and entity-type entities. Also the refine loop for the Discover chat.
notes: For the first turn send only `query` (plus optional limits). For each refine turn (change location, add a place, adjust topics and similar), call this same endpoint again and add `prior_query`, `prior_entities`, `prior_context` and `session_id`, each copied verbatim from the previous response.
Each parsed entity carries `value`, `type`, `confidence`, `normalized_value`, `aliases`, `metadata` and `languages`.

fields.prior_query: Refine turns only: previous turn's `query` string, verbatim.
fields.prior_entities: Refine turns only: previous turn's `parsed_entities` object, verbatim.
fields.prior_context: Refine turns only: previous turn's `context_report` string, verbatim.
fields.session_id: Refine turns only: previous turn's response `session_id`, verbatim.

200.text: Parsed query. Pass `session_id` on to `POST /pipelines` and on to the next refine turn.

GET /locations/v1/locations.desc: Search locations already in Ubiquity by name (not a geocoder). Pages with limit and offset.
notes: Searches only locations that already exist in Ubiquity. It is not a geocoder, and a place that has not been added through the unified search / discovery workflow will not appear.
`q` filters by name, and `offset` pages through results with no overlap between pages.

200.text: Location matches, returned inside a double-nested envelope.

GET /locations/v1/locations/{location_uu.desc: Get a location object (may be a synthesized COMBINED- location).

200.text: The location.

fields.order_by: Field to sort by, for example `created_at`.

200.text: Array of pipeline objects. Shape of one element:

POST /locations/v1/pipelines.desc: Create a pipeline from an existing saved search and feed (step 3 of creation).
notes: Must follow `POST /saved-searches` and `POST /feeds`. Calling it alone fails with a 400 `{"error": "Feed not found"}`.
Creating a pipeline does not start discovery. Launching discovery is a separate, optional step (`PATCH` the pipeline, then `POST /jobs/create`).

fields.saved_search_id: Id from the preceding saved-searches POST.
fields.feed_id: Id from the preceding feeds POST.

GET /locations/v1/pipelines/{pipeline_id.desc: Get a pipeline: feed_id, agent_config, discovery_config, search_filters.

200.text: The pipeline object. Once settings are saved, `metadata` carries `agent_config` and `discovery_config`; the object also exposes `feed_id` and `search_filters`.

PUT /locations/v1/pipelines/{pipeline_id.desc: Full update, for example a rename.

200.text: The updated pipeline object.

PATCH /locations/v1/pipelines/{pipeline_.desc: Update metadata.agent_config and discovery_config. This is the Agent Settings save call; resend the whole metadata object.
notes: The whole `metadata` object must be re-sent; a partial diff is not supported.
Quick Presets (Balanced, Social Media Boost, News Focus, Behavioral Datasets Boost) are client-side form state only. Nothing is stored until this call is made.
Also used right before `POST /jobs/create` to set `discovery_config` defaults.

Free-text instructions for the search generation agent.

200.text: The full updated pipeline object, with the new metadata.

GET /locations/v1/pipelines/{pipeline_id.desc: List routes (fan-in / fan-out) for a pipeline.

200.text: Array of routes. Source and destination pipeline names and feed_id are denormalized onto each one.

POST /locations/v1/pipelines/{pipeline_i.desc: Create a route from this pipeline to a destination pipeline.
notes: `filter_mode` and `filter_config` are accepted and stored. Their effect on what flows through the route is not documented yet.

fields.filter_mode: Defaults to `all`. Accepted and stored (for example `liked_only`). Effect on routing is not documented yet.
fields.filter_config: Defaults to `{}`. Accepted and stored. Effect on routing is not documented yet.

GET /locations/v1/organizations.desc: List the organizations the current user belongs to.
notes: Sharing targets must already be members of one of these organizations; arbitrary email invites are not supported.

200.text: Array of organizations. Most accounts see exactly one. Shape of one element:

GET /locations/v1/permissions/organizati.desc: List members of an organization: the only valid pipeline-sharing targets.
notes: Despite its name, `keycloak_user_id` here is the member's email, not a UUID. `ability` is the organization-level baseline, not access to a particular pipeline.

200.text: Array of organization members. Shape of one element:

GET /locations/v1/permissions/pipeline/{.desc: List current sharing grants for a pipeline.
notes: Same shape as the organization members response.

200.text: Array of current sharing grants, in the same shape as the organization members response:

PUT /locations/v1/permissions/pipeline/{.desc: Grant an organization member access to a pipeline.
notes: Send the email as a plain path segment, not URL-encoded.

The Share dialog grants `write` when Edit is checked, and `write` implies read. The value for view-only access is not documented yet; try `read` and check the result with `GET /permissions/pipeline/{pipeline_id}`.

fields.email: Target user's email, sent as a plain (not URL-encoded) path segment.
fields.ability: Use `write` (implies read). The value for view-only access is not documented yet.

200.text: Access granted.

POST /locations/api/v1/feeds.desc: Create the feed resource (step 2 of pipeline creation).
notes: Must run before `POST /pipelines`. The returned id is the numeric `feed_id` used throughout the API.

fields.metadata.description: Free-text description, for example `Feed for search: <query text>`.

GET /locations/api/v1/feeds/{feed_id}.desc: Get a feed, including its refresh interval.

200.text: The feed. Here the refresh interval is returned as a human-readable string.

PUT /locations/api/v1/feeds/{feed_id}.desc: Full update: rename, refresh and detection intervals, review settings. GET first and resend unchanged fields.
notes: Full PUT, not a partial update: omitted fields (including the feed's own `metadata`) are reset to null or default. GET the feed first and resend unchanged values.
`refresh_interval_minutes` is the same field behind the Enable Ubi toggle.

fields.name: Must be re-sent (full PUT).
fields.refresh_interval_minutes: 0 = do not update; 720 = 12 h; 1440 = daily; 2880 = every 2 days; 10080 = weekly; about 43200 = monthly.
fields.deletion_detection_interval_minutes: Settable by direct PUT. Effect on background jobs is not documented yet.
fields.engagement_detection_interval_minutes: Settable by direct PUT. Effect on background jobs is not documented yet.
fields.automatic_entity_rediscovery_interval_mi: Settable by direct PUT. Effect on background jobs is not documented yet.
fields.backdate_limit: int32. Probably a day count (unit not documented yet). A date string such as `YYYY-MM-DD` is rejected with a 400.

200.text: The updated feed. Interval fields come back as a struct.

GET /locations/api/v1/feeds/{feed_id}/me.desc: List metric generators for a feed.

200.text: Array of metric generators, or null when the feed has none. Shape of one element:

notes: `filter_prompt` and `filter_distance` are accepted and stored. Their effect is not documented yet.

fields.metric_name: Slug of `name`, generated by the client.
fields.filter_prompt: Intended as a semantic pre-filter that gates which artifacts get scored. Accepted and stored. Effect is not documented yet. May be null.
fields.filter_distance: Likely a vector-distance cutoff for that pre-filter. Accepted and stored. Effect is not documented yet. May be null.

200.text: Metric generator created.

PUT /locations/api/v1/feeds/{feed_id}/me.desc: Edit a metric generator (full PUT only).
notes: This resource takes full PUT only; there is no partial PATCH. Prefer this call over creating a replacement.

200.text: The updated metric generator.

GET /locations/api/v1/feeds/{feed_id}/st.desc: Direct Data Feed API: raw content items for the full corpus, with date, text, entity and URL filters, plus media asset metadata.
notes: Returns the full corpus with no 1000-item display cap, so it suits direct analysis of feed content.
Page through the corpus with `cursor`: pass `pagination.next_cursor` from each response back verbatim as `cursor` until `has_more` is false.

`media_assets` appears only on items whose source platform supports media capture; otherwise the key is absent (not an empty array). Use `GET /feeds/{feed_id}/media/{artifact_uuid}/{asset_id}` to download a stored asset.

fields.cursor: Opaque token (base64-encoded JSON) returned as `next_cursor` in the previous response. Pass it back verbatim; do not decode or construct it.
fields.order_by: `published_at` can be null (no usable date, or unparseable), and items with a null `published_at` are silently skipped under the default ordering. `scraped_at` is set at ingest and is never null. Use `order_by=scraped_at` to retrieve every artifact in the feed; the default ordering does not guarantee completeness. One of: `published_at`, `scraped_at`. Default: `published_at`.

200.text: A page of raw content items.
200.shape:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "uuid": "<string>",
      "headline": "<string>",
      "content": "<string, truncated to content_max_length>",
      "url": "<string>",
      "published_at": "<timestamp>",
      "scraped_at": "<timestamp>",
      "entity_id": <integer>,
      "entity_type": "<institution | individual>",
      "authors": [...],
      "metrics": {...},
      "media_assets": [
        {
          "asset_id": "<string>",
          "position": <integer>,
          "kind": "<image | video | thumbnail>",
          "status": "<stored | failed | unavailable_logged_out>",
          "source_url": "<string>",
          "storage_key": "<string>",
          "sha256": "<string>",
          "mime": "<string>",
          "bytes": <integer>,
          "duration_s": <number>
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "limit": <integer>,
    "total": <integer>,
    "has_more": <boolean>,
    "next_cursor": "<opaque string> | null"
  }
}

GET /locations/api/v1/feeds/{feed_id}/me.desc: Resolve a stored media asset from a stream item to a short-lived presigned download URL.
notes: Only assets with status `stored` can be retrieved. Find them in the `media_assets` list of an item from `GET /feeds/{feed_id}/stream`.
`artifact_uuid` is the stream item's own `uuid`, not its `entity_id`.
The returned URL expires after about 5 minutes; request a new one if needed.

fields.feed_id: Numeric feed id. It must be the feed the artifact belongs to: a different feed returns 404 "Artifact not found", and an unknown feed returns 400 "Feed not found".

200.text: Download link for the asset. The `url` is a presigned GET URL that needs no further auth and serves the raw file bytes directly.

404.text: Returned as `{"error": "Media not found"}` when the asset's status is `failed` or `unavailable_logged_out` (only `stored` assets can be served), or `{"error": "Artifact not found"}` when the `artifact_uuid` does not belong to the given feed.

400.text: Returned as `{"error": "Feed not found"}` when the `feed_id` does not exist.

POST /locations/api/v1/saved-searches.desc: Persist the parsed query and filters (step 1 of pipeline creation).

fields.name: Query text, used as the default pipeline name.
fields.search_filters.entities: Flattened `parsed_entities.locations` + `.topics` + `.entity_types` from the preceding `/search/unified` response, each entry's value/type/confidence/normalized_value/aliases/metadata/languages kept verbatim.

PUT /locations/api/v1/saved-searches/{sa.desc: Re-save a pipeline's search query and filters.

200.text: The updated saved-search object (same shape as the create response).

POST /locations/v1/entity-votes/toggle.desc: Like, dislike or flag an entity. Repeating the same vote type removes it.
notes: This is a true toggle: sending the same `vote_type` again removes the vote and returns `action: "removed"`.
`keycloak_user_id` here is the user UUID (the JWT `sub` claim), not the email. The chat endpoints use the opposite convention.

fields.keycloak_user_id: Keycloak user UUID (the JWT `sub` claim), not the email.

200.text: Vote removed (the same `vote_type` was sent twice).

GET /locations/v1/entity-votes/pipeline/.desc: List current votes for a pipeline.

200.text: Array of vote objects; `[]` if there are none.

GET /locations/api/v1/feeds/{feed_id}/en.desc: List discovered entities (sources and datasets) for a feed, with search, sort and type filters.
notes: A CSV export of a feed is built on the client by combining this call (`limit=1000`, `offset=0`) with `GET /entity-votes/pipeline/{pipeline_id}?limit=500`. There is no dedicated export endpoint.

fields.type: `sources` is documented; `datasets` is not documented yet (expected to follow the same pattern). One of: `all`, `sources`, `datasets`.

200.text: Page of entities plus counts.

DELETE /locations/api/v1/feeds/{feed_id}.desc: Remove an entity from a feed (hard delete).
notes: Hard delete; it cannot be undone.

200.text: Entity removed.

GET /locations/api/v1/entities/{entity_i.desc: AI-cluster an entity's source URLs by topic, as a preview before splitting. Slow.
notes: Slow (several seconds) because it uses AI clustering; use a generous timeout.
`is_keeper` does not reliably land on the group that matches the entity's name, so inspect each preview.
A "No split needed" result can occasionally appear under rapid repeated calls; retry if you expect a split.

200.text: Proposed grouping of the entity's sources.

POST /locations/api/v1/entities/{entity_.desc: Commit a previewed split. Destructive and cross-feed.
notes: Destructive and cross-feed. The original entity keeps the group marked `is_keeper` in the preview, and its name is not updated to match. Every other group becomes a new entity linked to every feed the original belonged to.

fields.groups: The groups returned by the preview, reduced to `group_name` and `source_ids`.

200.text: Split committed.

GET /locations/api/v1/entities/{entity_i.desc: Get a single entity's raw record.

200.text: The entity's raw record: location, metadata (base64-encoded) and timestamps.

GET /locations/api/v1/source-evaluation-.desc: Full AI evaluation reasoning for a discovered source, keyed by URL.

200.text: The AI evaluation of the source.

POST /locations/api/v1/feeds/{feed_id}/s.desc: Import a list of source URLs (plain text or CSV flows). Async, returns 202.
notes: Send either `urls` (plain text flow) or `urls_with_metadata` (CSV flow), not both. CSV parsing and preview happen on the client; this endpoint always receives the final URL list.
Returns 202 immediately. Progress polling for this `job_id` is not documented yet.

fields.urls: Plain Text sub-flow: array of raw URL strings.
fields.urls_with_metadata: CSV Upload sub-flow: array of `{url, name?}` objects, mutually exclusive with `urls`.

POST /orchestrator/workflows/dataset-upl.desc: Import a behavioral dataset (multipart: jsonl, csv or xlsx, up to 25 MB).
notes: Send as multipart form data with the form fields below plus the file (jsonl, csv or xlsx, up to 25 MB).
The name of the multipart part that carries the file is not documented yet.

fields.dataset_description: Optional free text for analysts and Ubi.
fields.dataset_external_id: Optional. Defaults to a value generated from the filename.

POST /orchestrator/workflows/dataset-upl.example:
dataset_title=<string>
dataset_behavior=consumer-spending
dataset_unit=Percent of 2019
dataset_source_url=https://example.com
dataset_description=<string>
dataset_external_id=<string>
<file part> (jsonl, csv or xlsx, max 25 MB; part name not documented yet)

200.text: Upload job created.

GET /orchestrator/workflows/dataset-uplo.desc: Poll a dataset upload job: pending, running, completed.
notes: Typical lifecycle: pending (progress 0.0), running (0.5), completed (1.0), reached within about 3 seconds for a trivial file.

200.text: Same shape as the trigger response. On completion `dataset_id` is populated, `series_names` lists the file's non-date column headers, and `observations_stored`, `skipped_rows` and `warnings` are filled in.

POST /orchestrator/api/v1/jobs/create.desc: Launch a discovery job. The only call that actually starts agentic work; optional relative to pipeline creation.
notes: Wait for a running job to finish before launching another for the same feed.
The request sends `job_type: "discovery"`; reading the job back reports `job_type: "curation"`. Both values are real.

fields.parameters.vote_context.liked_entities: Array of `{name, type}` objects used to steer discovery toward previously-liked entities.

200.text: Job created and queued.

GET /locations/api/v1/jobs/{job_id}.desc: Poll a job's status and progress.

200.text: Current job state.

notes: Only `status: "cancelled"` has been exercised.

200.text: The job, echoed with `status` set to `cancelled` and `completed_at` set.
Array of job objects (same shape as `GET /jobs/{job_id}`).
Total number of jobs.

fields.status: Job status to count. One of: `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`.

200.text: Number of jobs in that status.

GET /orchestrator/jobs/{job_id}/async-st.desc: Async sub-task progress for a job.

200.text: Progress of the job's asynchronous sub-tasks.

GET /understand/chat/sessions.desc: List Ubi chat sessions for a user and feed.
notes: `keycloak_user_id` is the account email here, the opposite of the entity-votes call.

fields.keycloak_user_id: The account email, not the Keycloak UUID.

200.text: `[]`, or an array of session objects. Each session's `filter_state` is derived automatically from its first message.

POST /understand/chat/sessions.desc: Create a chat session (created lazily on first message).
notes: The session is created lazily, on the first message, rather than when a dedicated "New Chat" action is clicked.

200.text: Session created.
The session.
Session deleted.
Array of messages, oldest to newest as stored.

POST /understand/chat/sessions/{session_.desc: Send a message to Ubi. Synchronous: the reply is in the same response. Required field: message.
notes: Synchronous: the reply comes back in this response and no polling is needed. A fresh session is created implicitly on the first call.
A trivial question takes about 3 to 4 seconds. Complex, feed-wide questions can take several minutes, so set a long client timeout.
This is a different chat system from the refine loop on `POST /search/unified`: this one is the standing per-feed Understand chat.

fields.message: Required. The field is `message`, not `content`; an empty body returns 422.

200.text: Ubi's reply, returned inline.

GET /understand/artifacts/count/{feed_id.desc: Count ingested artifacts for a feed. Preferred fast ingestion-progress check.
notes: A fast, inexpensive way to track ingestion progress; cheaper than reading `total_count` from `POST /artifacts/preview`.

200.text: Number of artifacts ingested for the feed.

POST /understand/artifacts/preview.desc: Fetch artifacts for the Data Browser. Capped at 1000 items regardless of limit.
notes: `limit` is accepted but ignored: at most 1000 items are ever returned.

fields.limit: Accepted but ignored; at most 1000 items are returned.

200.text: Up to 1000 matching artifacts.

500.text: Returned as "Collection <email> doesn't exist" before any artifacts have been ingested for the account. This is expected at that stage and is not a real failure.

POST /understand/metrics/preview.desc: Custom metric time series and per-artifact scores. Slow and uncapped; always scope by date range.
notes: No result cap, so it is slow (roughly 45 to 150+ seconds). Always scope the request with `filter_state.dateRange` and use a long timeout.

200.text: Time series plus per-artifact scores.
